subject: POC success criteria & evaluation plan — Atlas Payments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@atlaspayments.com>, Procurement <procurement@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC success criteria & evaluation plan \— Atlas Payments

Thanks again for the time today, Emma and Carlos \— good discussion on the integration surface and primary goals. Recap + proposed success criteria below so we have a shared starting point for the POC. Please call out anything you disagree with.

High-level POC scope (3-week trial):
- Integrate Redwood inference API with Atlas Payments sandbox (tokenized transactions routing)
- Evaluate latency, throughput, cost, and response quality on key prompts

Proposed success criteria / KPIs (baseline):
- Latency: P95 generation latency <= 250 ms (end-to-end) under expected load
- Throughput: sustained 40–60 requests/sec for typical request profile (avg seq length ~256 tokens)
- Cost: effective cost per 1k tokens <= $0.80 (i.e. <= $0.0008/token) with standard batching
- Quality: automated eval set (50 seed prompts) with >= 90% pass rate on business rules / no critical hallucinations; spot-check human review 4/5 acceptability

Evaluation plan (owner assignments):
- Redwood: integration support, telemetry, provide MOP and telemetry spec (attached: redwood_poc_mop_v1.pdf, poc-telemetry-spec.xlsx)  \— owner: Dev Patel
- Atlas: provide sandbox credentials, representative prompt set, and a small labeled eval set  \— owner: Emma Lopez
- CS (Redwood): run weekly syncs, collect results, and own mutual action plan  \— owner: Marissa Cole

Next steps:
1) Confirm the success criteria above (reply-all)
2) Sign the MOU / scope doc (I'll cc procurement for DocuSign)
3) Provide sandbox access + eval prompts by Oct 27
4) Redwood to provision trial capacity and share telemetry dashboard by Nov 1

Thanks \— I’ll put a brief MAP doc together and follow up with a DocuSign link.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@atlaspayments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlaspayments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & evaluation plan \— Atlas Payments

Thanks, Jordan \— solid recap. A few clarifications from our side: \
- Timeline: 3-week trial starting Nov 1 works for us. Procurement needs the MOU to review (please send).
- Latency: ideal is <=250 ms but we can accept up to 300 ms P95 during initial ramp if throughput is within target.
- Throughput: our baseline is ~50 req/sec during peak test windows; will try to provide a replay trace.
- Cost: procurement will flag anything above $1k/month for the trial \— your estimate helps but please include worst-case numbers.
- Data handling/Security: please attach SOC 2 pointers and a short note on data retention  \— our security team will request it.

I’ve looped in Procurement to expedite review. I can get the labeled eval prompts and sandbox credentials to you by Oct 27. Also attaching the signed MOU (see attachments).

— Emma
Emma Lopez
Head of Product | Atlas Payments

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@atlaspayments.com>, Procurement <procurement@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & evaluation plan \— Atlas Payments

Appreciate the quick reply, Emma. Attached the MOU for DocuSign and a slightly updated MOP (redwood_poc_mop_v1.pdf). Procurement  \— if you can kick off DocuSign with the attached MOU that would be great.

Per Emma's note, we'll treat 300 ms P95 as an acceptable ramp threshold but will aim for 250 ms target by week 2. We will also include a worst-case cost projection in the dashboard (Dev, can you add that?).

Marissa  \— can you own the weekly sync cadence and track the MAP milestones? I’ll set up the initial kickoff for Nov 1.

Regards,
Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement <procurement@atlaspayments.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & evaluation plan \— Atlas Payments

Thanks  \— I’ll take point on the MAP and weekly syncs. Here’s a concise evaluation plan I’ll follow and share as a living doc in the drive folder: \

Week 0 (pre-kickoff, by Oct 27):
- Atlas: provide sandbox creds, labeled eval prompts (50), and replay trace for throughput validation  \— owner: Emma
- Redwood: share telemetry spec (attached) and provision trial capacity  \— owner: Dev

Week 1 (integration):
- Smoke tests + end-to-end checks, validate telemetry, baseline latency/throughput numbers
- Owner: Dev / Jordan for coordination

Week 2 (stress & quality):
- Run throughput windows (50 req/sec), measure P95/P99 latency, token costs \
- Run automated evals + 10 human spot checks

Week 3 (handoff & decision):
- Final results, pass/fail on KPIs, remediation notes if needed, and next-step recommendation (pilot/expand/stop)

Acceptance criteria (summary):
- Pass if: latency P95 <= 300 ms AND throughput meets baseline AND quality pass-rate >= 85% (with remediation plan for failures)
- Stretch/ideal: latency P95 <= 250 ms AND quality >= 90%

I’ll publish the MAP and weekly agenda this afternoon. I’ll also include a link to the telemetry dashboard and an eval prompt sample (see poc-telemetry-spec.xlsx).

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlaspayments.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & evaluation plan \— Atlas Payments

Quick technical notes + checklist before Nov 1 kickoff: \
- Seq length / profile: please confirm expected avg and p95 token lengths (Emma)  \— assuming avg ~256, p95 ~512 for provisioning.
- Config recs: enable continuous batching with 200 ms batching window for best latency/cost tradeoff; use KV cache for repeated context to reduce tokens; try int8 quant for cheaper inference if model quality remains acceptable.
- Capacity: I’ll provision a dedicated GPU pool for the trial and expose a telemetry dashboard with P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, and cost/token.
- Estimated performance (for avg seq=256): P95 ~220–280 ms depending on load; throughput target ~50 req/sec sustained with autoscaling buffer.
- Cost estimate: ~ $0.0006–0.0009 per token depending on batch efficiency  \— will surface worst-case numbers in dashboard.

Action items for kickoff: \
1) Emma: confirm avg/p95 seq lengths and provide replay trace by Oct 27
2) Procurement: confirm signed MOU status in DocuSign
3) Jordan/Marissa: confirm weekly sync schedule (Marissa will send invite)

I’ll upload the telemetry spec and sample dashboards ahead of Nov 1 (attached: poc-telemetry-spec.xlsx).

-Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Software Engineer | Redwood Inference
